01 · Cover
Cue: Let the gate scene run while people sit down. Nothing to click.
Say: "Good morning. Today we follow one customer email and find out where your data really goes when you use AI at work. You will check your own Claude account, sort what people paste, and write one page."
Interaction: Ask one thing: where does your prompt go after you press Enter? Take two answers and do not answer.
Fallback: Quiet room? Ask a pair, not a person.

02 · The email
Cue: The email types itself, then the stamp lands. Right arrow once per sentence of the boss's draft. Vote with the TRUE, NOT TRUE and NOT SURE buttons (keys T, F, U). Backspace undoes the last click.
Say: "On Monday the biggest customer asks which AI tools we use and where its data goes. The boss drafts three sentences. Not all of them are true. Hands up for each one."
Interaction: Vote three times. Stay neutral and never reveal the answers. Sentence 2 is the one students will defend: let them. The counts come back on slide 12.
Fallback: No buttons? Count hands aloud and say the numbers.

03 · What really happens
Cue: Rings fill and the numbers count up. Right arrow: the 78 percent line. Right arrow again: the show of hands.
Say: "Most people already use AI at work, and few firms have rules. This is a survey of 604 German firms, not all firms. We have no number for North Macedonia."
Interaction: Hand up: used AI for work or study this week? Personal account, company account, both? Count with the buttons.
Fallback: One in four is 8 percent widespread plus 17 percent single cases; another 17 percent suspect it. Say survey of 604 German firms, never all firms.

04 · Send one prompt
Cue: The sketch shows the click path: New chat, paste, Enter, and the prompt leaves for the cloud. Right arrow ticks one check card each: plan, switch, chat on phone.
Say: "Send this prompt in your own Claude. Then check three things: your plan, the training switch, and whether the chat is on your phone. Look, do not change anything."
Interaction: Everyone sends and fills the line: Plan, Switch, Chat on phone. The Copy button copies the prompt. Labels may differ slightly; not found is a fine answer.
Fallback: Never open organization settings on a work login. A free sign-up with a personal email is fine and pairs are fine. With fewer than half logged in, share your own screen.

05 · Two rulebooks
Cue: Right arrow walks the plans: Free, Pro, Max, then Team, then Enterprise. Watch the route: the gate on the training line is a switch for personal plans and a lock for company plans. The eye opens from Team up. Click a segment to jump. Right arrow three: Anna question. Right arrow four: delete the practice chat.
Say: "Same prompt, different rulebook. On a personal plan, training is your setting. On Team and Enterprise it is not on by default, and the company gets an admin view."
Interaction: Finger vote on Anna: 1 personal, 2 company. Then everyone deletes the practice chat: hover, three dots, Delete.
Fallback: Never state the default of the switch: the page does not say. For Team say no fixed period stated and teach no number. No admin tools is derived from the plan pages; if asked about work-email linking, say check yours. Only the practice chat is deleted.

06 · Where it lives
Cue: Vote A, B or C first. Right arrow one: a prompt leaves the window and lands in your cloud account. Right arrow two: the folder, a wave marks every file as readable, the files Claude reads fly up. Right arrow three: the slide turns dark and the globe shows where chats are stored.
Say: "The app is a window. Your chats live in your cloud account. With Cowork you connect a folder. In cloud sessions, the files Claude opens are processed on Anthropic's servers. Stored in the US, processed in several places."
Interaction: Predict by tally first, then everyone writes: the vendor says my chats are stored in ____.
Fallback: What Desktop and Cowork send is our reading of the vendor pages: say check the vendor page. Folder access is a Cowork feature, not plain chat; admins can switch it off. Say the page offers no EU-only option, never that there is no EU option. EU regions exist on Amazon Bedrock and Google Cloud: that is the partner's hosting and contract.

07 · Right account, right data, right customer
Cue: Two presses per paste. First: the card drops in and the 20 second ring runs. Vote by dragging the card onto a lamp or by tapping a lamp (keys G, A, R). Second: the lamps flip and the reason types. Twelve presses in all; the last one shows the closing line.
Say: "Six people, six pastes. Green, amber or red? Decide on paper first. Yellow is a to-do list, not a permission."
Interaction: Decide six times; the room scores itself on paper. Scene 4 teaches the Desktop point. Scene 6 sets up the EU AI Act box on the next slides.
Fallback: Out of time? Do four scenes, not six. Enterprise does not turn red into green.

08 · Clean it by hand
Cue: One press: the four details lift out of the email and fly into their placeholders. The prompt card slides up.
Say: "If you paste it to clean it, you already pasted it. So clean it by hand, before you paste."
Interaction: Type the four placeholders into a notes app (3 minutes). Optionally run the prompt (2 minutes).
Fallback: Put real details back only in your own mail tool. No real data in the room. If time is short, Tim demos it.

09 · The EU AI Act in four boxes
Cue: The timeline builds one press at a time: banned, tell people, the Now pin, high-risk, everyday. Press 4 shows the guess. Press 5 shows five uses; then one press, or one click on a card, flies a use into its box and types the reason. Last press: the closing line.
Say: "Four boxes, three dates. Two boxes bind you today. The third starts 2 December 2027. A normal chat assistant is not high-risk, but GDPR still applies."
Interaction: Guess first by tally (A to D): where does a mood score sit? Then place the five uses by finger vote.
Fallback: No fines on slides. A chatbot makes you provider or deployer case by case, so say check your role. Outside the EU say can be covered, never are covered. The AI skills duty exists since 2 Feb 2025; Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 (in force 27 July 2026) changed its wording to take measures, not a guaranteed level. Banned: reading staff emotions at work. Short on time: three uses, not five.

10 · Ask in writing
Cue: Right arrow once per question; each one slides into the outbox. The last press adds the stamp and sends the plane. Click a question to count a vote; Copy the email copies all three.
Say: "This is the limits act. These are the things the pages do not say. So ask in writing, and re-read the vendor page on the day you send."
Interaction: In pairs pick the two questions your team needs most; copy the email.
Fallback: Say what we do not know: the Team retention period, EU storage for the chat apps, what Desktop sends exactly.

11 · Your page
Cue: The page draws itself and the six lines type in; the example sits in red. Right arrow one fades the example and starts the 6 minute ring. Right arrow two: swap, 3 minutes. Right arrow three: read your Never rule aloud, 1 minute.
Say: "Three sentences, three rules, on one page. Your own team, or Vardar Works if you have no job yet."
Interaction: Write 6 minutes on paper or notes. Swap 3 minutes: your neighbour marks one line unclear. Read your Never rule aloud 1 minute. 1 minute slack.
Fallback: Write from 1 December where a line is not true yet. Every amber gets an owner and a date.

12 · The end vote
Cue: The three sentences return with Friday's votes (left) and the new vote (right). Right arrow once per stamp. Right arrow four: the one page assembles itself from the answers. Right arrow five: your Monday step and the kit QR.
Say: "Back to Friday. Would you send it now?" Then the stamps. "Now we can send three sentences that are true."
Interaction: Vote again, then everyone writes one Monday step: Monday I will ____.
Fallback: Stamp 2 is the one that changes the most votes. The QR leads to the kit page with the zip.

A1 · Team vs Enterprise (appendix)
Cue: Right arrow reveals one row at a time. Use only if asked.
Say: "Both have single sign-on and admin controls. Enterprise adds SCIM, audit logs, the Compliance API and a delete timer. Neither uses chats for training by default."
Interaction: None.
Fallback: No prices and no seat numbers: they change, so re-read the live page.

A2 · If asked (appendix)
Cue: Static. Use only if asked.
Say: "Memory is on by default for personal plans; on Team and Enterprise an owner makes it available and each member turns it on. Connectors use your own permissions. Incognito chats are not saved to history or memory; on personal plans they are not used to improve Claude, on Team and Enterprise they still follow the org's retention."
Interaction: None.
Fallback: Say check your own account if you are not sure.
